look_here_first: CEREAL RYE is a cultivated/escaped INTRODUCED cool-season cereal grass with long narrow terminal spikes and rows of overlapping spikelets bearing long awns; each spikelet usually has two fertile florets. Contrast with Hordeum pusillum: true barley makes triads of 3 spikelets at rachis nodes. Rye is not a Hays-native restoration grass.

crew_field_check: Little barley (Hordeum pusillum) has triple spikelets at each rachis node and a much smaller tuft, whereas Secale cereale has a large continuous spike with individual 2-flowered spikelets alternating along the axis; distinguish from wheat Triticum aestivum by bract features, glumes and cereal head morphology.
